Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corp Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Lisa Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Lisa Thompson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corp's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are John Ramirez, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Harlan, Chief Operating Officer; Sarah Jenkins wait, no—David Patel, VP of Exploration; Emily Chen, VP of Marketing; Rachel Ortiz, Chief Sustainability Officer; and Tom Nguyen, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to John Ramirez.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Lisa, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corp delivered solid results in Q3 2024, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved record production levels averaging 152,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on exploration successes in the Permian and emerging international plays. We are focused on disciplined capital allocation to high-return drilling. Further, we are working on aggressive cost reductions in operating expenses. We continue to adjust to market dynamics with robust free cash flow generation. We are advancing our ESG commitments, including emissions reductions. We are evaluating bolt-on acquisitions to bolster inventory. Finally, we are taking steps to strengthen our balance sheet through deleveraging.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, John. As John mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $2.3 billion, up 22% year-over-year. Operating income was $950 million, and net income was $720 million. We generated $550 million in free cash flow and returned $300 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $12.4 billion in debt and $3.7 billion in cash.

Let me expand on our balance sheet strength, particularly our debt levels, net debt position, and leverage metrics, which continue to underscore our disciplined capital allocation amid a constructive macro environment with Brent averaging $82 per barrel and WTI at $78 in the quarter. We've made meaningful progress here, driven by robust free cash flow from our high-margin assets in the Permian and emerging Guyana positions, while maintaining ample liquidity and covenant headroom.

As of quarter-end, our total gross debt stood at $12.4 billion, down $850 million sequentially from Q2 and $2.1 billion year-over-year. This reflects proactive deleveraging, including the full repayment of our $500 million Term Loan B-3 facility—originally issued during the 2020 downturn at L+300bps—which we refinanced last year into lower-cost instruments. Our debt stack is well-laddered: 65% in fixed-rate, investment-grade unsecured notes with a blended coupon of 4.8%, maturing between 2026 and 2034; 25% in our revolving credit facility with just $1.2 billion drawn out of a $5 billion capacity at SOFR+175bps; and the balance in secured project financing for North Sea tie-backs, backed by strong offtake contracts with Equinor. Short-term debt is minimal at under 5%, providing flexibility amid OPEC+ decisions or Red Sea disruptions.

Our average debt maturity is 6.2 years, with no major maturities until 2026. We've locked in 70% of 2025 debt service at fixed rates through swaps, hedging Fed rate uncertainties. This compares favorably to peers like Occidental's heavier short-dated profile post-CrownRock.

Net debt, total gross debt less cash and equivalents, was $8.7 billion, down $1.1 billion quarter-over-quarter from $1.4 billion operating cash flow exceeding capex by $950 million—our strongest FCF since pre-COVID. Fueled by Permian output of 450,000 boe/d at 55% oil, D&C costs down 12% YoY to $650 per foot via optimized pad drilling and 12,500-foot laterals. Cash stood at $3.7 billion, including $1.2 billion restricted for Guyana FPSO with SBM Offshore.

Year-to-date, $2.8 billion FCF after dividends enabled $1.5 billion debt paydown and $800 million shareholder returns via 8% yield dividend and $400 million buybacks. This tracks our $8 billion net debt target by 2025 end, even at $70 Brent.

Leverage: net debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA improved to 1.6x from 1.9x Q2 and 2.4x YoY. Below 2.0x target, vs. EOG at 0.7x. LTM EBITDA $5.45 billion, up 18% on realizations and 8% volumes. RCF covenant 2.8x vs. 4.0x limit, interest coverage 6.5x. Debt-to-cap 28%, down from 35%, eyeing investment-grade with Moody's/S&P noting Guyana ramp to 150,000 bbl/d by 2027.

Permian leverage lowest at 1.2x, hedged $75 WTI floors. North Sea 2.1x mitigated by $300 million Harbour swaps. Guyana unlevered.

This fortifies growth: $4.5-5 billion FY24 capex for Permian pads at 20% IRRs $65 oil, Guyana FID. Capacity for M&A like $450 million DJ bolt-on. Stress-tested $60 Brent: leverage <2.5x, $3.5 billion FCF.

Now, turning to capital expenditures, breakdown across drilling, completion, facilities—budget vs. actual for first nine months. Full-year guidance $2.4 billion, 75% Permian. YTD spend $1.72 billion, 9.5% or $180 million under pro-rata $1.90 billion budget, from efficiencies amid inflation.

Drilling: budget $850 million vs. actual $780 million (8.2% under). 85 rigs: 55 Permian, 20 Eagle Ford, 10 Bakken. Permian Delaware Walker Ranch/Red Hills: 12.5 days/10k lateral via Nabors/Halliburton automation, 18 stages/day. Eagle Ford hybrid SAGD. Cost/foot $650, frame deals Tenaris/NOV.

Completion: $720 million budget vs. $680 million (5.6% under). 220 completions. Permian 'VanguardMax' zipper-frac 60/40 slickwater, 22 stages/day/fleet, Hi-Crush sand. Eagle Ford fewer clusters/dissolvable. IP30s track above curve. $45k/stage vs. $48k budget.

Facilities: $330 million vs. $260 million (21.2% under). Phased Permian solar 15 MW NextEra, Eagle JV infra. Bakken 85% recycling EPAL. GoM NGL terminal +$5 million.

Under-spend returns 60%+ FCF to shareholders. Banked $180 million Q4 bolt-ons. Full-year holds.

On operating expenses per BOE—or lifting costs in LOE—key to FCF. Q3 company-wide $8.50/BOE, 9% seq down from $9.35 Q4'23, 19% YoY from Q1'23. Three-year 31% reduction to lower quartile vs. peers. Q3 lifting $12.45/BOE, 14% YoY down $14.50, 5% seq from $13.10, 11th straight quarter down, -18% CAGR from $22.80 peak.

Trends: Q3'21 $20.15 inflation; '22 $14.50 normalization; '23 $12.45 tech/scale.

Drivers: digital AI Halliburton DecisionSpace 70% assets, downtime -25%, ESPs 620 days. Permian water recycle 85%, chemicals -18% Nalco. Vendor top 50 15% savings U.S. Steel/Tenaris. Eagle autonomous pads -40% headcount.

Regional: Permian $7.20 ($9.80 Q3 other), Bakken $10.50 ($15.50), GoM $14.80 ($22.40), Marcellus $6.80.

Target sub-$8 YE24, $7.50 '26. 10% OCF to innovation fund H2/CO2 fracs.

Permian digital Nexus Edge 80% pads ESPs 28 months, IoT tanks -22% hours, drones 60% inspections. Supply chain Halliburton/Liberty 10-15% off, SWD recycle 75% $0.65/bbl. 450 workovers $8/BOE, CT cleanouts. Headcount cross-train -18% idle.

Outlook Q4 $12-12.50, '24 $11.50 post-divest. Resilient < $50 WTI.

Production guidance: Q4 155-160k boe/d (3-6% seq up Q3 152k), oil 105-108k bbl/d, NGL 25-27k, gas 150-160 MMcf/d. FY24 152-155k, 8% up '23.

FY25 170-180k boe/d, 12-18% growth; oil 118-125k (70%), NGL 30-33k, gas 170-190 MMcf. Q1 low, Q4 185k.

Permian 110-115k (65%), 15% up, 30-well pads Second White Speckled IP30 1,800 boe/d simul-fracs 4,500 lb/ft, 12 DBC Q1 1.2 MMboe EUR. Service +5%, AI mapping 10 days/10k.

Eagle Ford 35-38k flat-5%, refracs 1,200 IP24h, G&P constraints midstream JV.

Bakken 18-20k, long laterals plug-perf.

GoM 7-8k, Winterfell 25% WI Q2'25 tie-backs.

Capex $1.2B D&C '25 flat, 120 wells 40% IRR $70WTI/$3.50HH, 65% oil hedged $72 collars. Digital twin Halliburton -15% cycles, nanoparticle EOR.

Macro OPEC+ $78-82, shale 13.4 MMbbl/d, LNG ramps. Risks LOE +7% labor, BLM delays; upside DBC 150, $200M Midland bolt-on.

50% FCF returns, 2.8% yield.

I will now turn the call over to Mike Harlan for an operational update.

Mike Harlan: Thank you, Sarah. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 152,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought the Black Mesa 12H-4 well online, which is expected to contribute significantly to our production growth in the coming quarters. We are also making progress on our cost reduction initiatives, leveraging scale and technology across our assets.

Now I will turn it over to David Patel for an update on our exploration activities.

David Patel: Thank you, Mike. We are excited about the potential of our exploration program. In Q3, we spudded 28 wells across our core acreage, brought online 32 gross wells, and maintained an average of 12 operated rigs running. This activity reflects our disciplined capital allocation, with D&C capex coming in at $285 million for the quarter—right in line with our guidance of $1.1 to $1.2 billion for the full year.

Key well results from flagship assets: Permian Basin, 65% inventory, Delaware Wolfcamp A/B Eddy/Lea NM. Black Mesa 12H-4, 12,800-ft Second Bone Spring IP-30 3,450 Boe/d 82% oil; norm 10k ft 2,700 Boe/d +18% type curve, +10% Pioneer. Five Wolfcamp C Northern Delaware avg 2,850 Boe/d 78% oil, 110 lb/ft prop, 3,500 lb/ft fluid, 52 stages diverters. Completions $7.2M/well -12% YoY bulk sand in-basin. EUR 1.4 Mboe/10k ft, DD&A 1.8x NTM EBITDAX. 98% success, 150+ 12k ft laterals, 7.5 yrs inventory, +25k acres Waha acquisition.

Eagle Ford South Texas $3.20 HH, eight Dimmit/Webb avg 1,950 Boe/d 72% liqs. Los Compadres 7H 2,400 Boe/d 68% oil 10,500 ft Lower EF, slickwater 100 mesh zonal, 18 days spud-rig -15%. Breakeven $45 WTI, 80% half-cycle $current.

Bakken Parshall four wells 1,120 Boe/d 85% oil type curve, offset interference, paused rig, 3.2 yrs Tier1.

Intl Namibia Orange Kavango-1X TotalEnergies 45 ft net pay turbidites >20% poro Sw<25%, 500 MMboe pot like Galp Mopane, Q1'25 flow test. $150M '25 offshore, Suriname 58 appraisal.

Differentials Permian $1.20 WTI Matterhorn/EPIC, EF $72/bbl net. 65% gas hedge '25. Seismic ML Palantir +22% hit rates +15% Tier1. Electric frac 80% Permian -40% em, flaring <1%. Recomps Bone Spring +250 Boe/d/well +2k locs.

'25 120-130 completions 14-16 rigs, Permian $1.4B 85 wells, EF $400M 35 wells. 15k laterals 48-well cubes. Expl $250M GoM wildcats Guyana. 8-10% growth 145k Boe/d '25 end $9,500/Boe top quartile. NDCM Permian 65-75% EF 55-65% $70 WTI. $500M dry powder M&A Devon-Concho style.

Drilling engine delivers high-return low-em barrels, $800M+ FCF '25.

Finally, I'll turn it over to Emily Chen to discuss our marketing strategy.

Emily Chen: Thank you, David. We are focused on optimizing our marketing strategy to maximize the value of our production. We are seeing strong demand for responsibly sourced LNG in Europe, and we are working to expand our customer base and strengthen our relationships with existing customers. The impact of this premium product is significant, capturing ESG-linked pricing uplifts amid EU CBAM pressures.

I will now turn it over to Rachel Ortiz to discuss our sustainability efforts.

Rachel Ortiz: Thank you, Emily. We are committed to reducing our environmental footprint and operating in a sustainable manner. Before diving deeper, let me provide a detailed update on our environmental performance around spills, incidents, and remediation, as maintaining world-class stewardship is core to our license to operate, especially with ESG investors like BlackRock scrutinizing metrics alongside FCF yield. Fiscal 2023 was our strongest, reportable spills down 44% YoY to 250 barrels, below API <1 bbl/MM produced. ROI on $450M multi-year sustainability capex.

15 reportable spills, -40% from 25 '22. Tier1 (<5bbl) 12 inc 120bbl Permian frac containment; Tier2 (5-1000) 3 inc 130bbl EF 45bbl 3rd-party; Tier3 zero 3rd yr. No GoM offshore BOEM SPCC. Vs Chevron 28 Tier1/2, Exxon Permian flat. US onshore 85% vol Permian produced water D&C $450/ft. GoM Ida '21 mooring zero spill '23. North Sea OSPAR Magnus crane 1 Tier1 skimmers. Guyana Stabroek Exxon/Hess flawless Liza2 ESG premium.

Remediation 100% closure avg 14 days vs 30 EPA. $15.2M 0.8% OpEx -39% '22. Bioremed 70% Permian microbes +25% faster; in-situ oxid EF diesel 95% BTEX 72hrs piezos; booms offshore 98% rec. 1200 GW samples 99.7% PAH non-detect. 85% natural atten RBCA -60% monitor.

"Zero by Design" Phase II: 5k IoT sensors 12k mi pipe Baker Hughes Cordant AI 95% predict +28% MTBF. Drones FLIR 40% Permian weekly, FracGuard pressure flags.

'24 $120M capex SLB Delfi predict. Mitigates spills, net-zero Scope1/2 2035 less flaring ins prem -15%. $75-80 WTI 20%+ ROCE de-risk SEC/EU CBAM.

Proud leader responsible production.

We have made significant progress on reducing greenhouse gas emissions and are investing in renewable projects, improving water and biodiversity.

Sustainability core to license, capital, value in energy transition. 2021 SBTi goals: 35% abs Scope1/2 cut 2030 from 2019 45M tCO2e, net-zero 2050. Methane intens <0.2% '25 OGCI, end routine flare '25 WB Zero.

H1'24 ahead: Scope1/2 -18% YoY 17.2M tCO2e, 22% below '19. Methane 0.15% -28%, flare 0.8% -1.4%. $1.2B low-C tech since '22 green bonds FCF $82 Brent.

Methane: Permian 1.2M acres OGI drones LEAP AI GHGSatSat 85% HP, 4500 leaks -32% fug. Gas capture 95% assoc 1.1M tCO2e/yr, 40% below 0.25% EDF. North Sea Buzzard VRUs 98% 250k t/yr, Rosebank Equinor subsea elec 1.5M t '26.

CCUS: Permian Hub Oxy DAC 5M t/yr '27 45Q $30-40/t. Qatar North Field LNG QatarEnergy 5M t 25% plant.

Efficiency: GoM 60% shore Entergy -15% Scope2. ADNOC Abu Dhabi Masdar solar 100% -40% diesel 180k t. 200 MW offshore wind Browse LNG Woodside.

Regional: US48 55% 8 kg/boe -25% Permian OPEC. NS 20% 12% down Johan2. ME/Aus 15% 5 kg. Guyana 15 kg flare ramp Stabroek zero Phase2.

Scope3 75% 3.2B t sold, 40% low-C refiners Chevron RDF. LNG book-claim 2M t EO Europe CBAM.

MSCI AA $500M sus loans -50bps. TCFD 10-K 2050 IEA NZE. Chal Scope3 LNG vol, CCUS steel +10%, but $80 oil $2-3B ann inv 15% ROCE.

22% Scope1/2 cut, methane/flare early, CCUS/elec/digital path 2030. Smart alloc premium multiple BlackRock/Vanguard.

I will now turn the call over to Tom Nguyen to discuss our technology initiatives.

Tom Nguyen: Thank you, Rachel. We are leveraging technology to improve operational efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance safety. We are investing in automation, data analytics, and AI to optimize operations, including Palantir Foundry for seismic ML boosting hit rates, electric frac fleets cutting emissions, and digital twins for cycle reductions. We are also exploring carbon capture and storage alongside predictive leak detection and drone inspections.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Alex Rivera with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on production guidance for next quarter and full year, including factors influencing projections?

John Ramirez: Good morning, Alex. As Sarah outlined, Q4 guidance is 155,000 to 160,000 boe/d, building to FY25 170,000-180,000 boe/d with Permian driving 15% growth via pad developments and DBC turn-ins. Key factors include capex discipline at $1.2 billion, hedging 65% oil at $72, and technical pilots like nanoparticle EOR, offset by service inflation and permitting risks, but upside from bolt-ons.

Operator: Our next question comes from Jordan Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Jordan Lee: Good morning. What are your expectations for debt levels and leverage going forward?

Sarah Jenkins: Thanks, Jordan. We're on track to $8 billion net debt by 2025 end, with current 1.6x net debt/EBITDA trending to 1.4x YE24 via FCF paydown. Laddered maturities, fixed rates, and regional low leverage in Permian position us resilient even at $60 Brent.

Operator: Our next question comes from Taylor Brooks with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

Taylor Brooks: Could you please provide more color on operating expenses per BOE trends and cost management?

Mike Harlan: Morning, Taylor. LOE at $8.50/BOE Q3, 19% YoY down, Permian $7.20 leading via digital predictive maintenance extending ESP life, water recycle, vendor deals. Initiatives like AI platforms, automation, workovers targeting sub-$8 YE24, enhancing FCF at scale.

Operator: Our next question comes from Chris Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Chris Patel: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

David Patel: Thanks, Chris. Strong IPs like Black Mesa 3,450 Boe/d and Namibia Kavango potential shift us toward 8-10% growth to 145k Boe/d '25, ramping rigs to 16, Permian focus 85 wells, $250M expl including Guyana/GoM. Adds inventory, supports FCF $800M+, M&A with dry powder.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lauren Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Lauren Kim: What is the outlook for the new product in the coming years?

Emily Chen: Good morning, Lauren. Responsibly sourced LNG to Europe sees strong demand, with book-and-claim certifying 2M tons, capturing premiums under CBAM. Outlook bright with LNG ramps, customer expansion targeting 40%+ low-carbon sales, bolstering realizations.

Operator: Our next question comes from Kevin Soto with Wells Fargo. Please go ahead.

Kevin Soto: Could you elaborate on your sustainability targets?

Rachel Ortiz: Thanks, Kevin. On track ahead for 35% Scope1/2 cut by 2030, already 22% below baseline; methane 0.15% beating 0.2% '25; flare <1%. Spills minimal 250bbl '23, 100% remediated. CCUS hubs, electrification, methane tech drive net-zero 2050.

Operator: Our next question comes from Nicole Grant with BMO Capital. Please go ahead.

Nicole Grant: What are the key technology initiatives you are focused on?

Tom Nguyen: Morning, Nicole. Prioritizing AI predictive analytics Palantir for sweet spots, IoT leak detection Cordant 95% accuracy, electric fracs -40% emissions, digital twins Halliburton for efficiency, drone FLIR, FracGuard—all cutting costs, boosting safety, supporting ESG.

Operator: Our next question comes from Brian Walsh with Piper Sandler. Please go ahead.

Brian Walsh: Can you expand on capex breakdown and budget performance?

Sarah Jenkins: Sure, Brian. YTD 9.5% under budget at $1.72B, drilling 8.2% under via faster cycles 12.5 days/lateral, completions 5.6% optimized fracs, facilities 21% deferred with solar electrification. Holds FY $2.4B, freeing FCF for returns.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to John Ramirez for closing remarks.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
